qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Unmatched Gulf Coast scale and high Nelson complexity index allow lowest operating costs per barrel among merchant refiners, but Valero is a complete commodity price-taker with zero pricing power over refined petroleum products and crack spreads.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Valero is a best-in-class low-cost Gulf Coast refiner, but operates as a structural commodity price-taker with zero independent pricing power. Profitability and ROIC fluctuate violently with global crack spreads (ROIC dropped to -3% in 2020 and normalized to ~7-10% in 2024 from the 2022 windfall peak), failing Munger's hurdle for enduring moat and pricing power >= inflation.
qualitative.evidence: Valero Energy operates 15 refineries with ~3.2M bpd throughput capacity and Diamond Green Diesel JV. Despite Nelson complexity advantages processing discounted heavy/sour crudes, earnings are governed by external crack spreads rather than pricing power: GAAP ROIC was -2.9% in 2020, 6.3% in 2021, spiked to ~30-40% in 2022 post-Ukraine windfall, and normalized to 7-10% in 2024 as net income fell from $8.8B (2023) to $2.8B (2024). Cash flows cannot be defended via price increases when crack spreads contract.
